title: WebSockets Examples
description: Each example belongs to one starter lesson. Follow its setup steps before trying it. These examples need the named tools and do not run in this site playground.

examples.title: Receive a welcome message
examples.description: The server sends text when a client connects. The client reads one message and closes.

examples.title: Send from the client
examples.description: The open event means the connection is ready. Sending before it is ready can fail.

examples.title: Return the same message
examples.description: An echo server sends received text back unchanged.

examples.title: Send structured message data
examples.description: JSON can give a message named fields. The server reads score and doubles it.

examples.title: Check a message shape
examples.description: A parsed object may still be missing a field. This example sends an empty object and gets a clear reply.

examples.title: Send to connected clients
examples.description: A broadcast visits each connected client. Only open sockets are ready to send.

examples.title: Check connection state
examples.description: readyState reports the current state. Inside open, it equals WebSocket.OPEN.

examples.title: Receive bytes
examples.description: A binary message carries bytes rather than text. This server sends three small byte values.

examples.title: Check that a peer responds
examples.description: Ping and pong are control messages. The ws client automatically answers a ping with pong.

examples.title: Close with a reason
examples.description: A close frame can carry a code and short reason. Code 1000 means a normal close.

examples.title: Handle unreadable JSON
examples.description: JSON.parse can fail. A catch block sends a friendly reply instead of crashing this handler.

examples.title: Limit message size
examples.description: maxPayload limits incoming message bytes. The client sends five bytes to a server limited to four.
